open_obligations: Check how Kirchner et al.'s PVG differs from Anil et al.'s game.
Check whether LLM training meets Kirchner et al.'s assumption that H is the set of all deterministic mappings from X to Z.
Check what conditions Kirchner et al. place on the prover's utility RP.

Check that Anil et al.'s condition, that the problem instance is revealed after the verifier picks its strategy, lines up with Kirchner et al.'s assumption that H is all deterministic mappings from X to Z.
Note that Anil et al.'s sufficiency argument assumes the verifier can switch to a complete and sound verification system; check whether Kirchner et al.'s Theorem 1 needs the same assumption.
out.other_title: PVG: verifier-leading Stackelberg equilibrium iff complete and sound protocol
out.rationale: Anil et al. prove verifier-leading Stackelberg equilibria are necessary and sufficient for complete and sound protocols in verifier-leading sequential PVG formulations where the problem instance is revealed after the verifier picks its strategy. Kirchner et al.'s Theorem 1 proves the same equivalence for a PVG with verifier utility RV and prover utility RP, assuming H is the set of all deterministic mappings from X to Z.
out.scope: proposed SAME_QUESTION_DIFFERENT_SETTING: verifier-leading Stackelberg equilibrium as the condition for completeness and soundness, in two prover-verifier games with different assumptions

text: The authors prove (Theorem 1) that, assuming H is the set of all deterministic mappings from X to Z, in the prover-verifier game with verifier utility RV and prover utility RP, the existence of a verifier-leading Stackelberg equilibrium (v*, h*, s*) is necessary and sufficient for the completeness and soundness properties to hold.
